derivation.auditor_key: (sk, pk) = DeriveKeyPair(SHA-256("edicta/policy/v1 test auditor|" + name)), RFC 9180 section 7.1.3; kid = SHA-256(tag("edicta/v1/auditor-kid") || pk)[0..16]
derivation.ephemeral_key: skE = DeriveKeyPair(SHA-256("edicta/policy/v1 test private ephemeral|" + label + "|" + index)).sk; index is the 0-based auditor position
derivation.aead_nonce: SHA-256("edicta/policy/v1 test private aead nonce|" + label)[0:12]
derivation.label: decimal plaintext_kind + "/" + record key hex
derivation.state_salt: SHA-256("edicta/policy/v1 test state salt|" + mandate label)
derivation.private_part_salt: SHA-256("edicta/policy/v1 test private part salt|" + commitment_hash hex)
derivation.note: Production draws all of these from a CSPRNG. Rejects reuse the PrivatePart envelope's randomness.

reject.description: Private form plus prev_state in clear (keys 13, 19, 20).
An allow with key 19 and without key 20.
Key 20 without key 19 (public form with key 20).
Private-form allow whose prev_state_hash is the genesis hash, with keys 15 and 16.
Private-form allow whose prev_state_hash is not the genesis hash, without keys 15 and 16.
Private-form deny with key 8 (reason) in clear.
Private-form allow with key 10 (facts) in clear.
Private-form allow with key 11 in clear.
Private-form allow with key 17: decided_at is in the PrivatePart.
Private-form deny with key 20: a deny's state read is private.

private_deny.description: A stage 4p deny (ErrAmountAboveMax, amount 6000 above 5000) of a private mandate: the public part has exactly keys 1 to 7 and 19, so every private deny has the same public shape; kind 9 under the path segment private; the rejection marker name ErrDenied.

blinding.description: One State (p4's state read): the public state_hash and the blinded state_hash_p under the counter's state_salt.
Genesis keeps the public constant under blinding.
Kind 15 key of a closed bucket in private mode.
Kind 15 key of a ClosedSet in private mode.
Equal PrivatePart content under two salts gives two private_hash values, so a public private_hash is no oracle for the content.

reject.description: An envelope of 65,537 bytes for plaintext kind 4, one above its cap: refused before decoding.
An envelope of 69,633 bytes for plaintext kind 5, one above the action cap.
The last ciphertext byte flipped: the DEK unwraps with a listed key, the AEAD fails.
Sealed with the core payload AEAD tag (edicta/v1/payload) as aad: the DEK unwraps, the AEAD fails.
DEK wrapped with the core HPKE info (edicta/v1/payload-dek): no entry unwraps with the policy info, so nothing opens.

cases.description: Private mandate; auditor-2's key opens the mandate, the PrivateParts, the closed bucket and the ClosedSets under their blinded keys; fast check and walk p4 -> genesis as in public mode, with the blinded state hashes.
No auditor key: step 1 (allow record, signature, binding, mandate_ref) runs; the rest is policy_private.
A key the envelopes do not list (auditor-3): nothing opens, policy_private.
The record under p4's private_hash opens to another PrivatePart: its hash differs from the key, source_corrupt.
Full walk without the key: L1 and L2 on public fields (keys 14 and 20, compared bytewise without the salt) down to the genesis hash; gate_integrity unchecked (policy_private), never ok.
No key; the gate signed amount 100, the action bytes say 1000. The facts are in the PrivatePart, so without a key the comparison does not run: unchecked (policy_private).
The same with auditor-1's key: the merged verdict's facts differ from the re-extraction, fail.
No key; anchor_time 60 s after the verified T_ref, hidden in the PrivatePart: unchecked (policy_private).
The same with a key: fail.
The PrivatePart opens and hashes to private_hash, but its state does not hash to the signed prev_state_hash (key 20) under the mandate's state_salt.
The gate blinded the state hashes with another salt than the mandate's state_salt: with a key, state_hash_p(prev_state) differs from key 20.

An allow whose PrivatePart, which hashes to the signed private_hash, also carries key 8 (a deny reason): the presence rule fails, so the gate signed a contradiction. The facts and state it does carry allow: policy pass, gate_integrity violated (gate_signed_inconsistent_private_part), exit 5.

An allow whose PrivatePart lacks key 10 (facts): the verifier's own extraction of the action bytes stands in and allows: policy pass, gate_integrity violated (gate_signed_inconsistent_private_part), exit 5.

The gate allowed amount 6000 (above the per-action maximum) and left the facts out of the PrivatePart: the verifier's own extraction denies, so the gate contradicts itself in a way that changes the outcome: policy fail (ErrAmountAboveMax), decision invalid, gate_integrity violated.
The mandate has auditors but the allow verdict is in public form (prev_state and facts in clear).
Two private-form allows with the same mandate_hash and the same prev_state_hash (genesis), different commitments; q1x is evidence. No key: the hash form of the fork rule.
Two consecutive private allows: without a key the walk compares c2's key 20 with c1's key 14 bytewise (L2) and reaches the genesis hash.
As chain_continuity_without_salt, but t2's key 20 does not equal t1's key 14: L2 fails without any key, violated.
